title: Protocol for the purification and transcriptomic analysis of mouse astrocytes using GFAT
protocol: Prepare mouse dissection area.
Place absorbent pad and set aside large blunt scissors, fine forceps, spring scissors, and spatula.
Pre-fill one syringe per animal with 0.4 mL of anesthetic solution.
Pre-fill 12-well plate with 4 mL glyoxal solution per well (one well per tissue processed).
Place all buffers and 12-well plate on ice.
Obtain mouse of interest, administer 400 μL of anesthetic intraperitoneally.
Wait until unresponsive to foot and tail pinch.
Perform cervical dislocation, remove the head with large scissors.
Remove head skin and muscle with operating scissors.
Open the skull by inserting fine butterfly scissors posterior of the cerebellum.
Cut along the midline and on each side of the brain.
Remove skull with fine forceps.
Obtain the brain with spatula.
Place brain in petri dish containing ice-cold 1X PBS.
Dissect cortex and cerebellum as fast as possible.
Place each dissected brain region inside one well of a 12-well plate pre-filled with 4 mL of ice-cold glyoxal fixation solution.
Mince tissue with scissors into fragments of approximately 9 mm³ in size.
Let plate with tissues sit on ice for 15 min.
Clean scissors with 70% ethanol cleaning solution after each tissue is processed.
Tilt plate at an angle of 45° and, with a P1000 pipette tip, remove as much glyoxal fixation solution as possible.
Perform 2x washes with ice-cold PBS: add 4 mL of PBS and remove as much of it as possible.
Repeat washing step twice.
Fixed tissues are now ready for homogenization and obtention of nuclei.
Transfer fixed and washed tissue pieces into Dounce homogenizer containing 3 mL NIM-T solution using forceps.
Use pestle A to homogenize tissue by gently sliding up and down 10 times or until tissue pieces are completely disaggregated.
Repeat the previous step using pestle B.
Replace pestle B.
Add 2 mL of 50% iodixanol to tissue suspension.
Mix 5 times with a P1000 pipette set to 500 μL.
Decant suspension onto cell strainer in a 50 mL conical tube.
Filter tissue suspension into the tube.
Replace strainer with cap and place on ice.
Transfer filtered tissue suspension into a high-speed centrifugation tube.
Load serological pipette with 2.5 mL 25% iodixanol.
Lower pipette to the bottom of the tube.
Very slowly, dispense 2.5 mL of 25% iodixanol below the tissue suspension.
Gently remove pipette to avoid disruption of the density gradient.
Spin down at 10,000 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant containing debris.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 1X PBS/1% BSA to the nuclei pellet.
Resuspend nuclei by pipetting 5 times with a P1000 pipette set to 0.5 mL.
Transfer nuclei suspension into a 1.6 mL micro-centrifuge tube.
Place nuclei suspension on ice.
Use 10 μL of nuclei suspension for nuclei counting with a hemocytometer or cell counter.
Stain nuclei with Hoechst by adding 2.5 μL of 2 mM Hoechst solution to each 1 mL of sample suspension.
Close the cap tightly and invert the tube 4 times.
Place on ice for 7 minutes.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and add 50 μL of Primary Antibody solution.
Mix with a pipette 5–10 times.
Place on ice for 1 hour (protect tubes from light by covering the ice bucket).
Add 450 μL of 1X PBS/1% BSA for the wash step.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and add 50 μL Secondary Antibody solution.
Mix with a pipette 5–10 times.
Place the sample on ice for 1 h.
Wash step: add 450 μL of 1X PBS/1% BSA and centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 μL of 1X PBS/1% BSA.
Use 10 μL of nuclei suspension for nuclei counting with a hemocytometer or cell counter.
Samples are ready for FACS-purification.
Set up BD FACSAria Fusion with a 70 μm nozzle.
Filter nuclei suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer and into a FACS tube right before sorting.
Sort Sox9+NeuN- and NeuN+ nuclei.
Collect purified nuclei into coated collection tubes placed in a
Place collection tray set to 4°C.
Sort samples and place tubes on ice after sorting.
Centrifuge collection tube at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C in a table-top centrifuge after all samples have been sorted.
Remove supernatant from the pellet, leaving 30-50 μL to avoid disrupting the pellet.
Add 350 μL of RLT buffer to each pellet and vortex for 30 seconds to lyse.
Obtain samples from -80°C freezer and thaw at room temperature for 10 min.
Perform RNA extraction with the RNeasy Micro Kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform on-column DNaseI digestion following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute RNA with 14 μL of molecular grade water warmed to 65°C.
Apply elution solution to the center of the membrane inside the column.
Let sit for 5 min before eluting by centrifugation.
Store RNA at −80°C or proceed directly to the next section.
Thaw RNA samples on ice for 10 min.
Perform reverse transcriptase reaction with Superscript IV VILO using 7 μL of total RNA.
After RT reaction, store cDNA at −20°C or use it for subsequent quantitative PCR (qPCR).
Thaw SYBR Green PCR Master Mix on ice for 10 minutes.
Obtain primers for genes of interest and reference genes.
Set up qPCR reaction according to specified volumes per well.
Perform technical duplicates or triplicates per biological sample.
Run qPCR and melt curve analysis adjusted to primers of interest.
Obtain cortex and cerebellar nuclei suspensions from 3-month-old mice after glyoxal fixation.
Stain the obtained nuclei suspensions as detailed in Figure 4.
Gate Hoechst+ and single nuclei according to details provided in Figure 4A.
Draw gates around Sox9+NeuN- and Sox9-NeuN- nuclei for FACS purification of astrocytes and non-neuronal populations, respectively.
Confirm post-sort nuclei purity for both populations as detailed in Figure 4B.
Extract RNA from each sorted sample following the procedure described in step 4.
Normalize CT values for each gene to Actb or Rplp0 CT and to the average of the control group (Sox9-NeuN- non-astrocytes) using the 2-ΔΔCT method.
Depict Sox9-NeuN- samples with squares and Sox9+ astrocytes with circles in gene expression analysis.
Employ technical duplicates for qPCR analysis.
Thaw RNA samples on ice for 10 minutes before proceeding if stored at -80°C.
Assess RNA quality and quantity using TapeStation (high sensitivity RNA tape) or Bioanalyzer following manufacturer’s instructions.
